title: THE BARYON-TO-DARK CLOSURE: does the framework predict Omega_b/Omega_m (0.157) or take it as input?  The provenance audit, the prediction attempt (M_sat / pie / equilibrium / flatness slack), the honest input count, and the verdicts.

V1_f_b_provenance.statement: THE f_b PROVENANCE: INPUT, EVERYWHERE.  The audit chain: (a) G052's flatness 'closure' derives Omega_dm = 1 - Omega_L - Omega_b from a MEASURED Omega_b (the lane's own words -- 'Omega_b measured'); (b) G079/G187 hardcode Omega_b = 0.0493 (Planck, 'published, not computed here') into the EH98 transfer and the envelope; (c) the pie's s_b(M) nods [0.081, 0.068, 0.1443, 0.2025, 0.2217] are MEASURED group/cluster baryon shares; (d) G178's 0.081 is the GROUP baryon floor (G143's E11 f_gas,500 + 0.02 stars), a cluster-scale measurement at 52% of the cosmic f_b = 0.156 -- NOT Omega_b/Omega_m and NOT derived; (e) the per-object M_b (measured M/L + gas) normalizes the BTFR, the equipartition and the dust law at every scale.  Zero derivations of f_b on the committed record.  The machinery is baryon-NORMALIZED: M_dark = M_b x dimensionless multipliers everywhere.

V2_derived_vs_input_count.statement: THE DERIVED-VS-INPUT COUNT: derived {m = 5.09 +- 0.10 keV (G212), M_sat = 3.09e14 (band [1.73, 4.01]e14), Z, s_Lambda, T_b, the u(M) exponent +0.314, q -> -1/3, A_b = 0.650}; identity-pinned {a0 = c^2/(Z R_dS) = 9.3624e-11 at ratio 1.00005 (Z11) AND empirically zero-point calibrated (S09), Omega_Lambda = 32 pi a0^2/(3 H0^2 c^2) (G058 algebra, G03C-flagged circular)}; measured inputs {G, c, H0, Omega_Lambda, Omega_m, OMEGA_B -> f_b = 0.1564, Omega_star, n_s, sigma_8, T_CMB, per-object M_b}.  In the six-core framing (a0, G, c, Omega_Lambda, f_b, m): 4 measured, 1 identity-pinned, 1 derived.  f_b sits in the MEASURED column; every closure point consumes it, none produces it.

V3_honest_statement.statement: HONEST -- the baryon fraction is the framework's last undeclared input, and the honest input count admits it: 6 core (a0, G, c, Omega_Lambda, f_b, m) of which 4 are measured cosmological constants (f_b = 0.157 among them) + 5 ancillary measured datums (H0, Omega_star, n_s, sigma_8, T_CMB) + per-object M_b.  The 'zero-free-parameter' claim is TRUE per object (closed forms given M_b and a0) and NOT a claim about cosmic inputs.  The closed sector's only f_b-adjacent emissions: (i) the halo baryon share <s_b> = 0.085 = 0.54 x f_b -- halo CONTENT from the measured nods, depleted, not a cosmic derivation; (ii) the flatness-slack echo f_b^slack = 0.160 vs 0.156 (2.3% at the committed Omega_L) -- an identity on measured sides (G03C class: you must input Omega_dm and Omega_Lambda to get f_b out), carrying the registered 0.6-0.9% slack of the committed Planck registers.  The machinery fixes the DARK-internal split (M_sat, f_dust, phantom share 1-f_dust = 0.33 median) and the dark-to-baryon ratio field (1:1 at r_M, x(R500/r_M) phantom gain, f_dark 6-10 clusters), never the baryon abundance: f_b = 0.157 enters the pie as the number that makes the dark sector measurable, and no test of the framework constrains it -- the last undeclared free parameter of the cosmic frame.
V3_honest_statement.one_line: the baryon fraction is the framework's input at every committed closure point -- the last undeclared free parameter of the cosmic frame (measured datum, not fit); the machinery emits only the halo baryon share 0.085 (depleted content) and the flatness-slack echo 0.160 (identity, G03C class)
